function.name: finance_calculator_npv
function.description: Calculate the Net Present Value (NPV) for a series of cash flows discounted at a certain interest rate. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

discount_rate.description: The annual interest rate used to discount the cash flows. This is a float type value.

years.description: A list of years when the cash flow occurs. Default is empty array.

message.reasoning:
We need to calculate NPV for cash flows [-50k, 10k, 15k, 20k, 25k, 30k] with discount rate 8% per year. Years default empty array means we assume consecutive years starting from year 0? Usually first cash flow at time 0. So year 0: -50000, year1: 10000, year2: 15000, year3: 20000, year4: 25000, year5: 30000. Discount each future CF by (1+rate)^t. Compute present values:

Year0 PV = -50000.

Year1 PV = 10000 / 1.08^1 = 10000/1.08 ≈ 9259.2593.

Year2 PV = 15000 / 1.08^2 = 15000/(1.1664) ≈ 12855. (Compute precisely: 15000/1.1664=12856.7)

Year3 PV = 20000 / 1.08^3 = 20000/(1.259712) ≈ 15878. (20000/1.259712=15877.9)

Year4 PV = 25000 / 1.08^4 = 25000/(1.360489) ≈ 18371. (25000/1.360489=18370.9)

Year5 PV = 30000 / 1.08^5 = 30000/(1.469328) ≈ 20418. (30000/1.469328=20417.9)

Sum PVs: -50000 + 9259.26 + 12856.7 + 15877.9 + 18370.9 + 20417.9 = Let's sum positives: 9259.26+12856.7=22115.96; +15877.9=37993.86; +18370.9=56364.76; +20417.9=76782.66. Subtract 50000 gives 26782.66. So NPV ≈ $26,783. Alternatively if discounting from year1 onward but initial negative not discounted. So answer ~26,800. Provide result. Use function? We can call the function.
